title: Bugs Roberts hired as arranger in 1937
summary: Wanting someone to write for the band, Pillars hires Bugs Roberts from Cincinnati at a weekly salary; he writes erratically and then joins Andy Kirk.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: Now getting back, to '36, we go through '36, with the personnel we told you about, into '37. In 1937, I felt a need that the band should have somebody to write for it. We didn't have anyone in the band or anyone in town that we thought that could write exactly what we wanted, you know, the style that we wanted. So a dance team came through here from Cincinnati, and they had some music -- I noticed the music was real pretty, and it was beautifully arranged, so I asked

them who made the music. And he mentioned, 'Oh man, there's a fella out from -- out in Cincinnati, named Bugs Roberts.' Said, 'Man, he can write his can off, you know? Just one of those kind of things. And they gave me Bugs Roberts' address, and I wrote Bugs Roberts and we gave him a proposition, to put him on a salary, all he had to do was write two -- two arrangements a week, you know.

And we sent for him. And Bugs came out, first week he wrote two. Two, dynamite tunes for us. Next week, he almost wrote two, the next week, he wrote one, the next week 'Why, I didn't quite get it finished,' you know, one of those kind of things, you know. But we paid him. And Bugs worked with us through the late winter, that's January, February, March, and April and that summer Bugs got a job with Andy Kirk. Andy Kirk was playing at the -- in Chicago, at the Grand Terrace.
